- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 3–8% in subsequent days to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates decline; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% to match sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates long-term (30d) price trends when sentiment is rising; add 1–3% bias upward for horizon >14 days if sentiment >0.6.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 5-day average (e.g., <avg-3%), consider upward bias correction to avoid underestimating momentum.
- For sentiment history showing increasing volatility (e.g., alternating highs/lows), reduce forecast smoothing and allow for 2–5% asymmetric adjustment toward sentiment peaks.
